correctness.summary: The five structural conclusions follow correctly from the cited Faraco–Rungi inputs. Global geometrizability makes d(rho) finite. Parity forces every realized total degree to have the same parity, while repeated holonomy-preserving bubbling from a minimal realization supplies every larger degree of that parity, giving D(rho)=d(rho)+2N. For fixed total degree m there are finitely many signatures, and each fixed-signature holonomy image is open, so both the exact-degree locus R_m and sublevel U_m={d<=m} are open. In any nonempty open set O, the integer set d(O) has a minimum m; O∩U_m is then a nonempty open set on which d is identically m. Hence the locally constant locus is open dense without a Baire assumption. A point with d=r>0 is non-locally-constant exactly when every neighborhood meets U_{r-1}, yielding the stated union-of-boundaries jump locus; r=0 is locally constant because U_0 is open. Finally, choosing one minimal signature per point and taking a finite subcover proves the compact finite-signature-bank statement.

limitations: The theorem does not compute d(rho) for non-Hitchin representations.
It classifies total branching degree, not individual branch signatures.
No effective global degree bound, neighborhood radius, or explicit jump-locus description is obtained.
The result is a short consequence of a very recent source, so later source revisions or parallel notes may overlap.

originality.summary: Faraco–Rungi's September 2026 preprint supplies all four substantive geometric inputs and explicitly frames minimal branching degree for non-Hitchin representations as an open direction. Le Fils provides important complex-projective precedent for minimal-degree and prescribed-branch questions. Current searches did not locate the saturated total-degree ray, upper semicontinuity, generic local constancy, boundary description, or compact finite-signature bank for the real-projective setting. The contribution is therefore supported as a clean topological synthesis of very recent source results, not as a solution of the underlying minimal-degree computation problem.

scientific_value.summary: Although d(rho) itself remains unknown in the non-Hitchin case, the result determines the whole total-degree spectrum once that single integer is known and proves that the unknown complexity is generically locally stable. The compact-family finite signature bank is a useful qualitative uniformity statement.
